text: Kanghan's heir is not amused. She didn't ask about his husk.
Moon Ahin, twenty-two: an A-rank summoner called the Puppeteer, and heir to Kanghan's guild. She stands over the abyss like she owns it.
Jaeha's visor fogs up from the inside.
From the top of a pipe, Nib gives him a flat stare.
She's here to inspect the surveys. Show her what her family pays for. Yes, Miss Moon, at once.
She walks past the crew. They sell their lives for less than one of her husks costs.
Then they must be very good husks, Jaeha says politely. Very brave husks.
Moon Ahin doesn't laugh. Ho does, and Woo elbows him.
One flick of her baton, and her column forms up behind number four. Walk, and spare her the jokes.
Down they go: Jaeha and his dull husk in front, then Moon Ahin, forty husks, and the crew.
She asks what a number has to write. It helps him count, he says. Traps, steps, husks.
How many of hers did he count? Forty. But they only have one rhythm.
Two rows of feet hit the steel at once. One body, one step, and one bad stone under it.
Then a shriek like tearing metal echoes across the canyon.
A dozen canyon wyverns pour out of the far wall and dive, beaks full of needle teeth.
One flick, and forty husks lock into a shield wall, shoving the crew behind them.
White fists punch the wyverns out of the air, three at a time.
Moon Ahin conducts with small, quick strokes, her face perfectly calm.
But the wall marches onto an old stone ledge, right over a live trap plate. Jaeha shouts. Quiet, number.
The ledge drops away, and three husks fall into the abyss, still in perfect formation.
Her face stays composed. One eyebrow twitches.
Through the gap, a wyvern snatches Ho and hauls him out over the drop. Woo grabs for his boot and misses.
Jaeha decides in a heartbeat. Everyone comes back, even if it costs him the mask.
Nib launches off the pipe in field form, amber blazing, long knives out.
One stroke, and the wyvern bursts into ash. Ho drops back into Woo's arms.
The rest of the flock wheels round for another pass.
Jaeha steps up beside her. The stones whose spiral opens left are live traps. Why listen to a number? Because she just lost three.
She hates it. The left ones, he said?
The plan: single file, right spirals only, and bait the dive onto one marked stone.
The husks cross single file. Jaeha calls the steps, and Moon Ahin conducts to his calls.
A tail barb rakes Nib's shoulder, and the gash opens on Jaeha's. He keeps calling.
Then his plain husk steps onto the marked stone as the whole flock dives at it, and stone spikes punch out of the wall through every one of them.
Ash drifts down like snow. The last two wyverns flee.
Ho lies on his back, laughing hysterically. He's alive. Wings of Glory lives.
Jaeha releases Nib early, back to rest form.
But Moon Ahin studies Nib up close. Husks don't move like that.
Then she flips Jaeha's respirator off with the tip of her baton.
Kang Jaeha. The trap-tester from the stream. He smiles weakly. Good evening, ma'am.
Four visors swing his way. He's the one who put Mok in jail? And Ho decides Wings of Glory has a mascot.
The foreman storms up. Whose husk was that? Hers, says Moon Ahin, without blinking. And number four is now her guide.
Quietly, she wants to know why he's in her family's gate. Same reason as her, he says. To see what's at the bottom.
Then walk, number four. And keep counting.
Down they go, the crew close behind Jaeha now, and a faint violet glow runs inside the pipes.
In ten years, Uncle Pyo never asked what the pipes were for. Tonight, they find out.
Pyo's hand on the rail trembles with a deep, slow vibration.
Down at the river, Lyra decides the woman in white is pretty, so she doesn't like her. She never likes anyone prettier, says Borro. Nobody is prettier, says Lyra. That's why.
The wall here is carved: a giant in coral armour holding back a wave with a trident, sea-people kneeling below.
Nib knows those markings: sea-people carving a hero. So why is a sea hero this far inland?
At the next landing, a locked steel gate guards a narrow cleft, with violet light pulsing deep inside.
Level four is engineers only, the foreman pleads. Director Baek's level. Moon Ahin is the inspection. Open it.
Very quietly: open. It.
His shaking hand unlocks the padlock.
Jaeha and Moon Ahin step into the cleft first, side by side, the pipes glowing violet beside them.
Then everything shakes. Dust falls, and forty polished heads tilt up together.
A huge pulse of violet light rolls up from below, the pipes swell like veins, and far down, something vast rises and falls.
Moon Ahin's grip tightens on her baton. Jaeha pulls his respirator off to listen.
At the canyon floor, through Borro's eyes, the river ripples in perfect rings with every beat.
Forty beats a minute. That's no machine.
That's a heart, as big as a building.
